name: Empirical and Hybrid Models

# Empirical and Hybrid Models
## Overview
Empirical and Hybrid Models provide non-physical or semi-physical approximations for volumetric light transport, prioritizing visual fidelity and performance over strict adherence to the Radiative Transfer Equation (RTE) [G]. Unlike physically accurate methods that solve for [multiple scattering](#12474-multiple-scattering.md), these models use heuristic shading terms, blurred indirect light, or hybrid surface-volume [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) to simulate translucency and atmospheric effects at interactive rates [G]. They set themselves apart from [Absorption-only model](839-absorption-only-model.md) by including scattering-like effects, and from [Single Scattering Models](15290-single-scattering-models.md) by avoiding the computational cost of exact integration, often relying on precomputed gradients or empirical blur operations [G].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Empirical Translucent Volume Shading](4109-empirical-translucent-volume-shading.md)
An interactive optical model that captures the qualitative appearance of translucency by blending direct attenuation with a [blurred indirect light contribution](#4092-empirical-volume-shading-with-indirect-light-approximation.md) and surface shading [Empirical Translucent Volume Shading](4109-empirical-translucent-volume-shading.md). It solves the problem of rendering semi-transparent data with realistic lighting without simulating multiple scattering [Empirical Translucent Volume Shading](4109-empirical-translucent-volume-shading.md). Choose this when interactive rates are required for complex optical properties where physical accuracy is secondary to visual appeal [Empirical Translucent Volume Shading](4109-empirical-translucent-volume-shading.md).

### [Hybrid Surface-Volume Rendering](12114-hybrid-surface-volume-rendering.md)
A method for visualizing CFD data that combines physically-based atmospheric attenuation for low-albedo gases with a scanline-buffer algorithm for surface-defined objects [Hybrid Surface-Volume Rendering](12114-hybrid-surface-volume-rendering.md). It sets itself apart by explicitly integrating surface fragments into the volume traversal loop to determine rendering extent, displaying the entirety of 3D data rather than just [isosurfaces](#13788-isosurfaces.md) [Hybrid Surface-Volume Rendering](12114-hybrid-surface-volume-rendering.md). Choose this when rendering mixed scenes with both dense volumetric gas and solid geometric objects [Hybrid Surface-Volume Rendering](12114-hybrid-surface-volume-rendering.md).

### Multi-Volume Illumination Rendering
A rendering approach using separate volumes for emission, absorption, and reflection to simulate material light properties, with gradients computed on the fly by the GPU [S1]. It allows for fine-grained control over voxel properties using scaling factors ($k_{em}, k_{ab}, k_{ref}$) and boolean masks [S1]. It is chosen for detailed visualization of specific tissue types or markers in medical/scientific data where distinct light [interaction](#41-interaction.md) properties need to be highlighted [S1]. The method sets emission and absorption volumes to the same data source, sets the reflection volume to a constant value of 1 for each voxel, and applies scaling factors globally or per-voxel [S1]. Boolean operations with masks select areas of interest for targeted voxel manipulation [S1]. Square root normalization is applied to combined volumes to amplify visibility after inversion, and final images are inverted to enhance print quality and contrast [S1]. [Stereo rendering](#10724-stereo-rendering.md) is optionally enabled by offsetting the camera along the x-axis to generate anaglyph images [S1]. The implementation uses a LUT resolution of $64 \times 64 \times 64$, a Henyey–Greenstein [phase function](#3111-phase-function.md) with asymmetry parameter $g = 0.8$, a focal length of 3.0 scene units, a distance to object of 6 scene units, and an opacity threshold of 0.95 [S1].

## Background
The concepts stem from the need for real-time or near-real-time visualization of complex volumetric data, such as medical imaging (e.g., zebrafish embryos, brain tumors) and CFD simulations [S1, Hybrid Surface-Volume Rendering](12114-hybrid-surface-volume-rendering.md). The specific implementations cited originate from research published in *Digital* (2024) regarding GPU-enabled volume rendering [S1]. The hybrid approach addresses limitations of traditional [isosurface rendering](#7669-isosurface-rendering.md) by capturing the full volume extent [Hybrid Surface-Volume Rendering](12114-hybrid-surface-volume-rendering.md). The empirical model addresses the computational bottleneck of multiple scattering by using heuristic approximations [Empirical Translucent Volume Shading](4109-empirical-translucent-volume-shading.md).

## Sources
